Theme 097 · Camera & edit grammar

Speed Ramp

Time itself is the edit. The hook fast-forwards a whole week of dashboards at 8×, the drop snaps to real time for the reveal, and the proof moment ramps down to ¼ speed so the viewer watches the human decide frame by frame. A speed graph like an editor’s time-remap curve runs under every frame, with a playhead showing where we are.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Speed graph — dark time-remap strip (8× / 1× / ¼×) with a coral playhead; the film’s spine
  • Speed readout — huge mono 8× / 1× / ¼× numeral in the corner, instantly readable
  • Echo frames — ghosted copies of moving UI showing fast-forward
  • Day chips — MON–FRI ticker that proves time is passing
  • Cursor onion trail — 4 fading cursors showing slow-motion movement toward the decision
  • Resolution chip — “Resolved in 6 min” green chip that closes the time story

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Fast-forward — 8× section: every UI update lands on eighth notes (0.25 s at 120 BPM), linear ease, echo trails 5 frames deep
  • Ramp knee — 8× → 1× in 6 frames with a custom bezier (0.9, 0, 0.1, 1) so the change lands exactly on the drop; kick drum = snap
  • Slow-mo hold — 1× → ¼× over one bar (2 s, sine.inOut) into the proof, hold ¼× for 12 s, ramp back over one bar; graduated steps (1–2–4–2–1) feel natural

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A speed ramp tells the product story without words: humans live in fast-forward (too many dashboards), Pulse brings real time, and the critical decision deserves slow motion. It works with plain screen recordings and adds drama cheaply. Risk: in a still, speed needs visual proof (echoes, a readout), and a long slow section drags.

Adapt to your product: Record your product doing real work, then fast-forward the busywork your users do today and ramp down to slow motion on the one moment your product changes (the click, the approval, the result). The speed graph works with any product.

References: https://morphic.com/ai-glossary/speed-ramping (speed ramping: smooth speed changes within one shot) · https://www.kapwing.com/resources/how-to-use-the-speed-ramp-effect/ (graduated 1×–2×–4×–2×–1× ramps for smooth acceleration)
